title: Integrative Proteome and Metabolomics Analyses of Cryptococcus neoformans Responses to Melanin Substrates Niger seed and L-DOPA
projectDescription: Melanin, as a pivotal antioxidant pigment, plays a critical role in the pathogenicity of Cryptococcus neoformans. However, the underlying signaling pathways responsible for melanin biosynthesis in C. neoformans are not yet fully elucidated. In this study, proteome and metabolomics analyses were conducted to investigate the response of C. neoformans to melanin substrate Niger seed or L-DOPA. The proteome analysis identified significant differential expression of proteins in cells treated with Niger seed compared to L-DOPA, with distinct functional enrichment patterns observed. Subcellular localization analysis showed unique protein distribution in cells treated with each substrate. Metabolomics analysis revealed distinct metabolic profiles in response to Niger seed or L-DOPA, with notable differences in metabolite regulation between the two treatments. KEGG classification highlighted specific metabolic pathways affected by each substrate. Overall, this study provides valuable insights into the complex regulatory mechanisms underlying C. neoformans response to melanin substrates.
sampleProcessingProtocol: In this study, the wild-type strain of Cryptococcus neoformans var. grubii H99 was utilized. Three independent cultures were grown in 50 ml of YPD medium (2% glucose) at 30°C for 16 hours with shaking at 110 rpm. After incubation, the cells were washed with phosphate-buffered saline (PBS) and adjusted to a concentration of 5.0 x 108 cells in 50 ml of melanin induction medium, which included either Niger seed medium or L-DOPA medium. These cultures underwent dark incubation at 30°C for 6 hours and were subsequently centrifuged, with cell pellets washed and stored at -80°C. For proteome analysis, cell pellets were ground in liquid nitrogen and resuspended in a lysis buffer containing TritonX-100 and protease inhibitors. Following sonication and phase separation via centrifugation, protein precipitation was performed using ammonium sulfate-saturated methanol. The precipitated proteins were washed, reconstituted in 8 M urea, and quantified using a BCA kit. For trypsin digestion, trichloroacetic acid was added for protein precipitation, followed by washing and dissolution in triethylammonium bicarbonate. Trypsin was added for overnight digestion. The resulting peptides were purified and analyzed using a ThermoFisher Scientific EASY-nLC 1200 UPLC system and an Orbitrap Exploris 480 mass spectrometer. The data were analyzed with DIA-NN software, matching tandem mass spectra against a C. neoformans var. grubii H99 database for protein identification and quantification.
dataProcessingProtocol: The analysis of DIA data was performed using version 1.8 of the DIA-NN search engine, with tandem mass spectra matched against the C. neoformans var. grubii H99 database, which contains 7429 entries. A reverse decoy database was included for accuracy, employing Trypsin/P as the cleavage enzyme with allowance for one missed cleavage. Fixed modifications included N-terminal Met excision and carbamidomethylation on Cys, with a false discovery rate (FDR) set below 1%. Gene Ontology (GO) analysis was conducted to categorize proteins based on biological processes, cellular components, and molecular functions. Software tools like eggnog-mapper were utilized to extract GO IDs from identified proteins, facilitating functional classification and annotation. For pathway analysis, the Kyoto Encyclopedia of Genes and Genomes (KEGG) was used to identify protein pathways through BLAST comparisons, focusing on biological processes such as metabolism and cellular functions. Subcellular localization of proteins was predicted using WolF PSORT, which helps sort proteins into various eukaryotic compartments. Functional enrichment of differentially expressed proteins was evaluated using Fisher's exact test, with significant terms exhibiting fold enrichment over 1.5 or under 0.67 and a p-value less than 0.05. Finally, hierarchical clustering based on functional classifications was performed using a transformed p-value matrix, applying Euclidean distance and average linkage clustering in Genesis software. The resulting clusters were visualized with heat maps created using the R package "ComplexHeatmap."
keywords: Cryptococcus neoformans; melanin biosynthesis; substrate-dependent manner; substrate-independent manner
